old: Long ago, this word could mean almost any fruit — or even the round orb of an eye.
Its ties to sin come from a pun: a Latin word for this fruit sounded just like the Latin word for evil.
German speakers still call it Apfel, and Swedes say äpple — cousins of the very word you're guessing.
clues: This orchard fruit has a name that, in Old English, could mean any fruit at all, and figuratively even an eyeball or a sphere.
Crisp and round with red, green or yellow skin, it lacks the pear's tapered neck and is the classic fruit for pies, cider and teachers' desks.
Genesis never names Eden's forbidden fruit; it likely became this one because Latin words for it and for evil looked alike. One a day keeps the doctor away.
